q: A friend says, 'The Torah explains that G-d chose Avraham because he discovered G-d as a child.' What is the best correction?
opts: That idea comes from Exodus 1
The Torah says Avraham was the richest man
That idea comes from Rambam, not Genesis
The Torah says G-d chose Lot first
exp: Genesis 12 is silent; Rambam and the midrash fill the gap.

q: Avraham argues with G-d to save strangers but rises early to obey when told to offer his son. Which statement is most accurate?
opts: His responses differ by situation
He always argues with G-d
He never questions or challenges G-d at all
He argues only for his own family
exp: Use the five stories as evidence.

q: Which situation is a covenant rather than a command?
opts: A ruler orders subjects to pay a tax
Both sides promise something and keep it over time
A person decides privately to believe
A one-time sale with no future contact between buyer and seller

q: Why is brit milah important in your notes about Avraham?
opts: It was a law at Sinai
It was Pharaoh's command
It replaced belief in G-d with a ritual
It is the sign of the covenant
exp: Your notes: brit milah is the covenant; maybe the first Jew.
why: It adds a sign to belief.

q: Which person is NOT one of Yaakov's 12 sons?
opts: Levi
Gad
Esau
Naphtali

q: The Israelites have grown and Pharaoh calls them a 'people,' but they have no land or laws of their own. What are they?
opts: A people, not yet a nation
A family of 70 persons
A nation with a government
A kingdom of priests already
why: They have grown far beyond that.
They have no government of their own.

q: Why did Joseph make his brothers swear to carry up his bones?
opts: He wanted to be buried in Goshen
He expected G-d to bring them back
He planned to rule Canaan himself
He feared Pharaoh would take his bones away

q: Which event added shared laws to the Israelites' nationhood?
opts: Leaving Egypt under Pharaoh
Crossing the sea on dry land after leaving Egypt
Entering the land with Joshua
Receiving the Ten Commandments

q: A post says, 'Everyone who attends that protest supports Hamas.' What is the main problem?
opts: It criticizes a government policy fairly
It quotes the Torah incorrectly
It overgeneralizes from some to all
It uses too many statistics

q: The largest party has 27 seats. Can it govern alone?
opts: No, it needs 61 with partners
Yes, the largest party always governs
Yes, if the president approves it
No, because 27 is over the threshold

q: What was the stated purpose of the mandate system after World War I?
opts: Return the land to the Ottomans
Help a people prepare to rule itself
Make Britain rule the land forever as a colony
Create the Knesset right away
why: It was meant to be temporary.

q: Some Turkish Jews used sugar instead of honey on Rosh Hashanah. What does this show?
opts: They rejected the wish for a sweet year
The Torah banned honey
Every Jewish community around the world copied them
The meaning stayed while the form changed
